notes: The four italic words carried over from v20 are one `added` unit; no morpheme in this verse licenses any of them, and the italics only corroborate (rule 7).
`אֲשֶׁר` plus the resumptive suffix fuses in *whose*, headed on the relative (rules 22, 30).

One defensible alternative was not noted on its unit: the *in* of *hedged in* could be read as the rendering of `בַּעַד` rather than as an English phrasal particle, which would leave that preposition aligned instead of unrepresented under rule 40. What was taken is the phrasal-verb reading, on which *in* names nothing on its own (rule 44).
